answer: Payout tracks storage rank, not keys. Each epoch it codes a corpus into shards, one per identity, kept online. Credit equals the rank its shard adds to the set already held: a thousand wallets holding one shard add one rank, so the farm collapses. Spot checks demand random linear combinations, so stale copies prove nothing, and each shard has one custodian, so duplication shows. The fable that aliases multiply influence meets a ferrous fact: copies weigh nothing. Attackers must buy distinct disk and bandwidth, answering random challenges through every tide of load, costs rising, payout flat.
